title: Suspected Dementia: Memory Assessment and Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult initial cognitive assessment, reversible-factor review, collateral history, imaging selection and referral for subtype diagnosis.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national dementia guideline was identified in the sources opened on 14 October 2026. NICE guidance is an international comparator pending Saudi/local adaptation.
SFDA product registration was not verified; any medicine selection requires the current Saudi Drug Information register and hospital formulary.
Local capacity, driving and safeguarding procedures require Saudi legal and organisational confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Neurodegeneration disrupts memory, language, executive or visuospatial networks. Different pathologies produce different cognitive and behavioural patterns. Delirium, depression, medicines and metabolic disease can mimic or worsen dementia. Diagnosis requires decline from prior function, not a low test score alone.
keyMechanisms: Neurodegeneration disrupts memory, language, executive or visuospatial networks.
Different pathologies produce different cognitive and behavioural patterns.
Delirium, depression, medicines and metabolic disease can mimic or worsen dementia.
Diagnosis requires decline from prior function, not a low test score alone.

symptoms: Progressive memory, language, planning, navigation, personality or daily-function change reported by the person or informant.
physicalSigns: Cognitive-domain deficit, functional decline, neurological signs, gait change or behavioural symptoms.
redFlags: Acute fluctuation, reduced consciousness, focal deficit, new seizure, head injury, infection or rapidly progressive decline needs urgent assessment.
precipitants: Vascular disease, neurological disease, anticholinergic/sedative medicines, alcohol and sensory impairment can contribute.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Acute fluctuating attention and arousal with a precipitating illness or medicine.
Mood syndrome may impair concentration; cognition should be reassessed after treatment.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Change from previous cognition and daily function
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Progressive decline corroborated by someone who knows the person
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Establish time course, domains affected and safety impact.
ruleIn.normalValue: No decline from previous cognitive or functional baseline

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Treat the contributor and reassess cognition.

ruleOut.normalValue: TSH and vitamin levels within local adult ranges

clinicalManagement.title: Separate delirium and neurological emergencies
actions: Use urgent assessment for acute fluctuation, reduced arousal, focal deficit, seizure, infection or rapid progression.
Assess immediate safety, self-neglect, exploitation, driving and medication management.

clinicalManagement.title: Complete initial assessment
actions: Take patient and collateral histories, assess function and mood, perform physical/neurological examination and use a validated cognitive tool.
Review medicines, sensory impairment, alcohol and obtain targeted blood tests.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer for specialist subtype diagnosis
clinicalManagement.timeframe: After reversible contributors are addressed and suspicion remains
actions: Refer to a specialist dementia diagnostic service and arrange structural imaging as appropriate.
Provide information, involve the chosen carer/advocate and record capacity and safeguarding needs.

medicationPlan.note: Do not start cognitive-enhancing or behavioural medicine before specialist subtype diagnosis and person-specific risk assessment.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Reversible causes investigated and dementia still suspected after initial assessment.

teaching.scope: Adult initial cognitive assessment, reversible-factor review, collateral history, imaging selection and referral for subtype diagnosis.
learningObjectives: Use collateral history and functional change alongside testing.
pitfalls: Missing safeguarding, driving or medicine-management risk.
keyPoints: A normal brief cognitive score does not exclude dementia.
Address reversible contributors before referral, without abandoning follow-up.

references.title: NICE NG97: Dementia: assessment, management and support

patientEducation: Explain assessment steps, uncertainty and support options to the person and chosen supporters.
lifestyleAndDiet: Support hearing/vision correction, activity, sleep, vascular-risk management and safe routines.
mdtReferrals: Memory service/geriatrics/neurology, primary care, pharmacy, occupational therapy and social/safeguarding services as needed.
dischargeCriteria: Urgent causes excluded, immediate safety addressed, tests reviewed and specialist referral with named follow-up owner recorded.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Track referral and review earlier for acute change, wandering, unsafe driving, self-neglect, falls or carer breakdown.
